bends.reason: B1 (seq 1): strip-side bend of the Z-joggle between the holed main plate and the narrower strip that carries the web (the CAD side-view label sits at the strip end of the joggle wall). Raw SIDE shows a crisp ~90 deg step: the wall is square to both plates, and the strip runs parallel to the main plate, offset from it, as in the CAD profile. Raw TOP shows the joggle line across the full strip width, and raw ISO shows the step band. Direction: REVERSE-direction bend, opposite to B2 (they form the Z-offset) and in the same sense as B4, as in the CAD. Judged from global views: the manifest marks this case STATE_CHECK with no section images.

B2 (seq 2): main-plate-side bend of the Z-joggle (the CAD side-view label sits where the holed plate meets the joggle wall). Raw SIDE shows the main plate turning ~90 deg into the joggle wall, which B1 then turns back, so the profile matches the CAD step. Raw TOP and ISO show the step along the full width. Direction: same sense as B3/B9 and opposite to B1/B4, matching the CAD.

B3 (seq 3): flange on the far edge of the holed main plate (the edge opposite the joggle). Raw SIDE shows the plate turning ~90 deg into a short flange, on the side away from the web as in the CAD. Raw FRONT shows that flange face-on as a full-width rounded band, and raw TOP shows it edge-on as a dark line along the whole top edge. Direction: same sense as B2/B9, opposite to B1/B4, matching the CAD.

B4 (seq 4): root bend of the large trapezoidal web along the strip's outer edge. Raw SIDE shows the web at ~90 deg to the strip. The two big outer tabs stay in the strip plane and run past the web line, exactly as in the CAD. Raw FRONT shows the web face-on with its central cut-out and two uncut centre tabs; raw TOP shows it edge-on as the dark line at the strip's outer edge. Direction: REVERSE-direction bend; the web turns opposite to the B3 flange (same sense as B1), matching the CAD.

B5 (seq 5): small foot flange at the end of one web leg (the right leg in the CAD TOP/FRONT views; in the side view it coincides with B6). Raw FRONT shows a dark edge-on bar at the end of BOTH legs, so neither leg continues in the web plane; only the uncut centre tabs extend further, as in the CAD. Raw TOP shows the face-on foot (with its small hole) beyond the web line at both leg positions. Raw SIDE shows the foot at ~90 deg to the web, pointing away from the plate. Direction: same sense as B6/B7/B8, opposite to B4, matching the CAD.

B6 (seq 6): small foot flange at the end of the other web leg (the left leg in the CAD TOP/FRONT views; its side-view label sits at the far end of the web). Raw FRONT shows edge-on foot bars at the ends of both legs. Raw TOP shows the face-on foot beyond the web line at both leg positions. Raw SIDE shows the foot at ~90 deg to the web, pointing outward away from the plate, as in the CAD. Direction: same sense as B5/B7/B8, opposite to B4.

B7 (seq 7): short tab beside the right relief opening in the strip, folded outward from the web just below the web root (the right twin of B8; in the side view it coincides with B8). Raw SIDE shows this stub at ~90 deg to the web, parallel to the strip and just below it, with nothing left standing in the web plane at the root. Raw TOP shows, at BOTH relief openings, a face-on tab ending just short of the foot tab under it. That double outline matches the CAD TOP at both positions. Direction: same sense as B5/B6/B8, opposite to B4, matching the CAD.

B8 (seq 8): short tab beside the left relief opening in the strip, folded outward from the web just below the web root (the side-view label sits on the web just past the B4 root). Raw SIDE shows the stub at ~90 deg to the web, parallel to and just below the strip, pointing away from the plate. Raw TOP shows, at the left relief opening, the face-on tab stacked over the B6 foot, the same double outline as the CAD TOP. Direction: same sense as B5/B6/B7, opposite to B4.

B9 (seq 9): return lip at the end of the B3 flange. Raw SIDE shows the flange turning a second ~90 deg back over the main plate, giving a C-shaped hook, with the lip parallel to the plate. Raw TOP shows the lip overlapping the plate edge, with its U-notch at mid-span where the denser two-layer region thins out, matching the U-notched lip outline in the CAD TOP. Direction: same sense as B3 (it completes the hook), matching the CAD.
